_comment: Template for scripts/memory-sync.sh. Copy to ~/.claude/memory-sync.json, fill in your shared org-tier repo, and add ~/.claude/memory-sync.json + ~/.claude/.memory-sync/ to your sync exclusions (never distribute this filled copy). See CLAUDE.md, 'Sharing instincts/memory across a team (org tier)'.

gate._comment: Shared by scripts/memory-sync.sh (promote path) and scripts/artifact-gate.sh (shipped-artifact sweep). ipAllowlist is a regex of IPv4 prefixes that are NOT reported, e.g. an internal VPN net. denyNames is the list of tenant and project names that must never appear in a shipped artifact or in promoted memory; it is matched case-insensitively as a literal substring, and the names themselves are never echoed into gate output. THE CRITERION IS NAMES THAT DO NOT BELONG IN THE SHARED REPOSITORY -- NOT NAMES THAT BELONG TO YOU. Your own organisation or namespace name must NOT be listed: it is the namespace the shared repository lives in, so it is present by construction in repo, repoUrl and every overlay.* path, and listing it refuses every promote onto every existing file -- a check that always says the same thing stops being read, and then nothing gets scanned at all. See handbook/system/discipline-gate.md, 'What belongs on the list -- and what must not'. Keep this file out of every repository -- putting the names into a tracked file would leak exactly what the check protects. A CI job that cannot read this file can pass the same list via the CCPR_GATE_DENY_NAMES environment variable (newline- or comma-separated) from its secret store.

conformance._comment: Read by scripts/conformance-run.sh (docs/adr/ADR-0010-conformance-runs-against-consumers.md). consumers is a list of real projects this operator maintains, addressed by LOCAL FILESYSTEM PATH ONLY -- nothing is ever fetched over a network. Each consumer's id is what reports show; the path never appears in a report unless --show-paths is given. optional (default false) means a missing path is reported as not-covered instead of failing the run -- useful for a consumer that lives on a machine this config is also used from, but is not always checked out. pins are concrete, dated, per-consumer expectations (class C3) -- each MUST carry a non-empty why, printed next to a violation, explaining why this consumer fact is CCPR behaviour rather than consumer content. A pin is exactly one of expectFinding (a substring, or a POSIX ERE when regex: true, that must appear on at least minCount report lines -- default 1) or expectField (one of exit, errors, warnings, info, filesScanned, compared against value -- filesScanned is a floor (>=), every other field is exact equality). Deliberately never a commit SHA, and never a fact about the CONSUMER's own working state either -- a pin's subject must be something CCPR controls, not something that changes the moment that consumer commits. Keep this file out of every repository, same reasoning as gate.denyNames above: a consumer's path is frequently a home directory.

pins.why: this consumer's own reserved-but-empty module directory (a .gitkeep only) must keep reporting as such; if this stops firing, either the module got built (fine) or phase-docs-lint's covers: emptiness check regressed (not fine)
this consumer's docs/memory/ is a frozen fixture and must stay clean against memory-lint

lint._comment: Read by scripts/manual-lint.sh check (g) (CCP-1151 stage 4 cut 4). forbiddenProse is a list of {term, tokenContexts, lineContains, pathContains} objects -- a project-specific terminology decision (e.g. a retired prose word your own project swept out) that must not ship hardcoded in the generic script. The default is empty: with nothing configured here (and no CCPR_LINT_FORBIDDEN_PROSE env var), check (g) checks nothing -- it never assumes any project's retired vocabulary. term is matched as a case-insensitive SUBSTRING in prose (markup included -- an occurrence inside an HTML comment is still read). An occurrence is excused (not an error) if ANY of the three lists match: tokenContexts excuses it when the text immediately preceding the match, case-insensitively, ends with one of these strings (a PREFIX check -- e.g. ["sub", "sub-"] excuses both a frozen `subskill` field key and the hyphenated `sub-skill` spelling alike); lineContains excuses it when the RAW line (case-sensitive substring) contains one of these phrases; pathContains excuses the WHOLE FILE for this term when its path, prefixed with the SCANNED ROOT's own directory name (never the file's full absolute path -- an ancestor directory above the root, e.g. a checkout path or username, must never silently widen what a substring excuses), contains one of these substrings (a protocol document, a fixture that pins a pre-sweep literal on purpose). A CI job that cannot read this file can pass the same list, as a JSON array, via the CCPR_LINT_FORBIDDEN_PROSE environment variable -- which REPLACES this key entirely rather than merging with it, same precedent as gate.denyNames/CCPR_GATE_DENY_NAMES above. Keep this file out of every repository, same reasoning as gate.denyNames: a retired-vocabulary decision is project-specific configuration, not shipped-artifact secrecy, but hardcoding it into the generic script would still make every downstream project inherit it. DO NOT GROW THE THREE LISTS TO SILENCE A FINDING: every entry EXCUSES an occurrence, so adding one LOOSENS the guard, and it is the only edit here that can let a real regression pass without a sound. When check (g) fires, the first question is whether the word belongs at that site at all -- widening an excuse is the cheapest way to green and the one that costs you the guard. Each entry wants a named reason behind it; a green run after adding one proves nothing, because a new entry produces exactly that by construction.

lineContains: <vendor filename or protocol phrase that legitimately contains the word>
